title: Universal 81/29 Bound for Tuza's Triangle-Cover Conjecture
description: Unconditional Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization proving 29 * tau(G) <= 81 * nu(G) (tau(G) <= (81 / 29) * nu(G) ~= 2.793103 * nu(G)) for every finite simple graph G, where nu(G) is the triangle packing number and tau(G) is the triangle transversal number, strictly improving Sichen Wang's 165/59 bound (arXiv:2609.13831). Coverage by this package's Palomar comparison: of the companion paper's 10 main results, 1 is compared in Lean in full (10%; Theorem 2, in natural-number, rational and explicit-transversal forms); Theorems 4, 5, 6 and 7 and Propositions 8, 9 and 10 are proved in this package's Lean library but not compared; Proposition 11 (the 32-vertex gadget) is by certificate only, checked in exact rational Python; Corollary 3 is by written proof only; Conjecture 1 (Tuza's conjecture) is open and not counted. Abstract claims: 1 of 9 compared in Lean (11%). Extends Wang's MIT-licensed sichen-wang/tuza-lean library with helper-arborescence coupling, unmerged colored-family covers, and opposite-edge elimination, together with non-vacuity checks nu(K_4) = 1 and tau(K_4) = 2. Generated and checked by AI research agents built and directed by Tyler B. Hughes. No human mathematician has yet refereed the proof.
